cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A bargee counts out the toll in coin so worn the faces are gone. It is two marks short. He says it is the toll his father paid.

left.label: His father's toll will do
left.outcome: He touches the worn coins to his cap.

right.label: The table is the table
right.outcome: He pays. He does not look at you again.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: Scrip again. The Company store takes it; my cellar does not. Whose money is the Keeper paid in, and whose is the town paid in?

left.label: Pay the hands in coin
left.outcome: Coffers lighter; the inn fuller.

right.label: Scrip is the Company's rule
right.outcome: "So is drowning, when it suits them."

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: A quarter's tolls in advance, at a small discount for the trouble. My principals like certainty. You would like a full chest. Everybody likes something.

left.label: Take the advance
left.outcome: The chest is full and the Book has a promise in it.

delayed_resources.message: Sorrel coal barges pass on tolls already paid.

right.label: Tolls at the gate, as ever
right.outcome: "Certainty. Fine. I'll find it elsewhere."

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: Marguerite Cole. I hold the chapel's lease and half the town's. I am told the Keeper's chest is light. I lend, kindly, on terms. Shall we discuss terms?

left.label: Discuss terms
left.outcome: Terms are one in ten, monthly, kindly.

right.label: The chest will manage
right.outcome: "Of course. My door is always open. It has a bell."

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: The toll table has not been revised since Year 58. The Board has authorized a rise of one part in twelve. For the record, the Board did not say when.

left.label: Raise it now
left.outcome: The queue learns of it at the gate. Loudly.

right.label: After the season
right.outcome: "Noted. The Board will ask why."

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: The bargee offers the toll and, folded under it, a second coin for the Keeper personally. He does not say why. He does not look as if he needs to.

left.label: Pocket it
left.outcome: The second coin is heavier than the first.

right.label: Into the Book, both coins
right.outcome: He shrugs. Someone else will pay it next time.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The moot wants to know why the mooring fee on the pound went up. I told them to ask you. Here I am, asking you, on their behalf, at my own inn.

left.label: The Company set it
left.outcome: "Your Company. Noted, as she says."

right.label: Waive it for townsfolk
right.outcome: The moot approves. The Book does not.

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: Fun fact: your toll on empty return barges is higher than on full ones. Somebody wrote that in Year 12 and nobody has read it since. I have read it.

left.label: Correct the table
left.outcome: Empties pay less. Sorrel's fleet sends more empties.

right.label: The table stands
right.outcome: "Then I'll fill my empties with something cheap."

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: The interest is due. I do not send men. I send reminders, and then I send the Company a copy of the note. Which would you prefer to receive?

left.label: Pay the interest
left.outcome: "Kindly. Same time next month."

right.label: Send the copy
right.outcome: Vosk receives it. Vosk reads everything.

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: There is a gap in the Book between the fourth and fifth bells of the last watch. Vessels passed. Nothing was written. You will find I have to ask.

left.label: The hands forgot
left.outcome: "Noted. The hands do not keep the Book."

right.label: My error; here are the tolls
right.outcome: You make up the sum from your own pocket. She notes that too.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A Hullfolk boat offers to pay its toll in smoked fish. The fish is very good. The toll table does not have a column for fish.

left.label: Fish is a toll
left.outcome: The Company store is briefly the best-smelling building in Halfway.

right.label: Coin or scrip
right.outcome: They find coin, somewhere, slowly.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The hands were paid short this watch. Dace says the chest was light. Dace says you said so. Is the town going to hear about it at the moot or at my bar?

left.label: Make up the wages from tolls
left.outcome: The Book has a hole. The hands have their beer.

right.label: Short until the season turns
right.outcome: "Then they'll work short too."

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: I can pay this quarter's fees in Sorrel bonds. They are as good as coin in Sorrel. This is not Sorrel, I grant you. Yet.

left.label: Bonds at a discount
left.outcome: Paper in the chest. It rustles.

delayed_resources.message: The Sorrel bonds are worth less this month.

right.label: Coin
right.outcome: "Fine. Coin. Delay costs, and this cost you."

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: A gift for the Keeper's house: a good chair, from my own parlor. No terms at all. I like to see the post well kept.

left.label: Accept the chair
left.outcome: It is a very good chair. You think about it more than a chair deserves.

right.label: Decline, kindly
right.outcome: "Of course. It will be here."

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: The chest is heavier than the Book explains. Not by much. Enough. I am not asking where it came from. I am telling you I have noticed.

left.label: Bank the difference with the Company
left.outcome: "Noted. That was the correct answer."

right.label: Spend it on the gates
right.outcome: Quenn is delighted. Vosk writes a line.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: The toll chest's lock has been forced in the night. Nothing is missing. Somebody wanted to know what was in it, or wanted you to know they could.

left.label: New lock, no report
left.outcome: Tamm fits a lock that would stop a bear.

right.label: Report it to the Company
right.outcome: Vosk arrives within the hour and looks at the lock a long time.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: A Sorrel bargee tried to pay for his supper in your Company's scrip, which I don't take, and then in a story about a Keeper who does. Is that Keeper you?

left.label: It is now; take scrip
left.outcome: "At half face. And you'll hear about it."

right.label: Your inn, your rules
right.outcome: "Good answer. He went hungry."

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: Aldmere's inspector has proposed a 'Compact levy' on Sorrel coal. It is not in the Compact. It is on your gate. I am asking you not to collect it.

left.label: Collect nothing not in the table
left.outcome: "Thank you. That's rarer than you'd think."

right.label: Collect it; let them argue
right.outcome: They argue for a month. The chest enjoys it.

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: The chapel's lease is due and Sister Hale has asked me for time. I am a patient woman. I am also a landlady. A word from the Keeper would settle which I am this month.

left.label: Give the chapel time
left.outcome: "For the Keeper. Kindly."

right.label: Business is business
right.outcome: Hale pays. The poor at the gate eat less that week.

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: The Board has asked for a statement of the summit's accounts for the Jubilee. I can write it accurately, or I can write it well. For the record, I am asking which.

left.label: Accurately
left.outcome: "Noted." She looks at you as if you had passed something.

right.label: Well
right.outcome: "Noted." The Board is pleased. She is not, quite.
